newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares close lower on EMU nervousness.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares close lower on EMU nervousness.

text.p: Italian shares closed lower on Friday after bond futures and the lira were weakened on a hectic day in which conflicting reports flew thick and fast over Italy's chances of qualifying for EMU membership.

The all-share Mibtel index closed 0.68 percent lower at 12,248 while the blue chip Mib30 index finished 0.85 percent down at 18,220. Investors also seized the opportunity to take profits after solid gains earlier in the week.
Mounting hopes that the Bank of Italy will cut the discount rate if preliminary April CPI data, due out next week, show inflation continuing to fall were not enough toi support the market.

Markets were unnerved after a budget commission in the lower house of parliament voted against a proposed 1997 mini-budget but brokers were confident that the government could win a confidence vote on the issue.

Fiat retreated 2.02 percent to 5,689 lire while ENI held steady, shedding just 0.75 percent to 8,813 lire. Olivetti finished 1.74 percent down at 497.2 lire ending a week of heavy losses triggered by announcement of a capital reconstruction plan.
Edison was among the day's gainers as investors took heart after the company's announcement on Thursday evening of a big jump in net consolidated profits.
Ambroveneto sank 2.41 percent to 4,254 lire, wiping out some of the big gains it made on Thursday when talk of a linkup with savings bank group Cariplo drove up the stock.
Clothes maker Stefanel was also down after its main shareholder said that reports of a takeover by HPI were without foundation.
Mobile phone operator TIM closed 1.02 percent lower on profit-taking, after a week of advances, at 5,111 lire.
